content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Thanks for sharing this. Before anything gets built, I'd like to understand what you're really after, so we shape the right thing.

To start with the "why":

When you picture this bookmark app being finished and working well, **what would be different from how you handle bookmarks today?** For example, is there something frustrating or missing right now that pushed you to want this?

And relatedly — **who is this mainly for?** Just you personally, or a group/team of people sharing bookmarks together?

Once I understand the goal behind it, I'll walk you through actual working screens one step at a time so you can react to something concrete rather than just talk in the abstract.

It’s mainly for me personally, not a team. My browser bookmarks have become a cluttered list, so I often can’t find something again or remember why I saved it.

I’d like one place where I can quickly save a link, organise it with tags, add a note for context, and later find it through search. I also want a clear distinction between things I still intend to read, things I’ve finished with, and things I want to keep but archive out of the way. Ideally, saving a link shouldn’t involve copying all its page details by hand.

We've now probed the empty, invalid, and large-collection edges across every part of the app, and each is settled. Before I propose building the real thing, one assumption I want to make explicit rather than silently bake in:

- **Your bookmarks are saved and stay there between visits.** Everything you save — links, tags, notes, their to-read/done/archived state — should still be there when you close the browser and come back later. (In the prototype the list resets on reload; only your sort/page-size preference persists. In the real app the bookmarks themselves would persist too.) Is that the expectation — a private store that's just yours and endures?

Here's where we've landed. **So far these flows are settled:**

1. **Quick saving** — paste a link, its title and description are fetched for you and are editable; add your own tags and a "why I saved it" note. Save even when a page can't be reached; incomplete links are flagged gently; pasting a link you already saved opens it for editing instead of duplicating.
2. **Three ways to hold a link** — *To read*, *Done*, and *Archived*, where archiving is separate from reading status and restoring returns a link to exactly where it was. Plus editing and permanent deletion.
3. **Finding things** — per-view search across title, link, description and note (case-insensitive), with a precise query language (`#tags`, `"exact phrases"`, `and`/`or`/`not`, parentheses) and click-a-tag filtering.
4. **Handling a big collection** — sort by date added or title, choose 10/25/50 per page, move through in groups, with your sort and page-size remembered.

One thing I've **set aside for later**: showing each site's real favicon and preview image (right now it's a coloured letter) — a visual polish item, not a change to how anything works.

**May I now start building this scope as the real application?** (I'll switch from exploring to implementing only once you say yes.)

Yes, I expect everything to be private to me and still there when I return. The four flows you summarized are right, but I’m not ready to start implementation yet because several important behaviours haven’t been explored.

In particular:

- When entering tags, I want suggestions from tags I already use.
- I need to select several bookmarks—or every bookmark matching the current search or view—and add/remove tags, mark read/unread, archive, or delete them together.
- Notes should support simple Markdown formatting and display it properly.
- I want a preserved copy of a page that I can revisit if the original changes or disappears. For a PDF, preserve the PDF itself. I’d also like the option to save a copy through the Internet Archive.
- I want to save useful combinations of search text and included or excluded tags for reuse.
- I need to import existing browser bookmarks and export my collection in the standard bookmark HTML format, keeping titles, tags, and original saved dates.
- Display preferences should include text size as well as the sort and number shown.

Also, the real favicon and preview image aren’t merely optional polish to me; they are part of the page information I expect the app to collect automatically and show with each bookmark.

Please walk me through these remaining behaviours before building the final application.

- **Genuine capabilities confirmed:** real page metadata is fetched server-side (verified against a live site), the favicon/preview image are collected and shown with letter/"no image" fallbacks, data is stored durably and privately on the server, and preserved copies are captured (the page as a local copy, PDFs as the file) with the optional Internet Archive link.

What each approved scenario maps to in code is recorded in `implementation/design/scenario-map.md`, with the design rationale in `decisions.md`.
